q: 1. The moment of inertia of a rectangular section 3 cm wide and 4 cm deep about X-X axis is
2. Moment of inertia of a circular section about its diameter (d) is
explain: The standard formula for the area moment of inertia of a circle about its centroidal axis (diameter) is πd⁴ / 64.

q: 3. Moment of inertia of a circular section about an axis perpendicular to the section is
explain: This refers to the Polar Moment of Inertia (J). According to the perpendicular axis theorem, J = Ixx + Iyy = πd⁴/64 + πd⁴/64 = πd⁴/32.

q: 4. Moment of inertia of a rectangular section having b = Width and d = Depth about x-axis is given by
explain: The standard formula for MI of a rectangle about its centroidal X-X axis (parallel to width b) is bd³/12.

q: 5. M.O.I. of a circular section of diameter d about an axis passing through its C.G. lying in the plane of the section is given by
explain: The Moment of Inertia of a circle about its diameter is πd⁴/64.

q: 6. The moment of resistance developed in a beam subjected to bending moment will, at any instant be
explain: For static equilibrium in a beam, the internal moment of resistance developed by the stresses in the cross-section must exactly balance the external bending moment applied at 그 section.

q: 7. A simply supported beam is subjected to a central concentrated load. The slope at the two ends is given by
explain: For a simply supported beam with a central load W, the maximum slope (θ) at the supports is WL² / 16EI.

q: 8. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load W. The maximum bending moment M is
explain: For a SS beam with total UDL 'W' (where W = w * L), the maximum bending moment at the center is WL/8 (or wL²/8).

q: 9. A simply supported beam of span L carries a concentrated load W at its mid-span. The maximum bending moment M is
explain: The maximum bending moment for a central point load on a simply supported beam occurs at the center and is equal to WL/4.

q: 10. A simply supported beam carries two equal concentrated loads W at distances L/3 from either support. The max BM is
explain: The reactions are W at each support. The BM between the two loads is constant and equal to Reaction * Distance = W * (L/3) = WL/3.

q: 11. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam of length L with a central load W, is
explain: Standard deflection formula for a SS beam with central point load: δ = WL³ / 48EI.

q: 12. The ratio of max deflections of a SS beam with an isolated central load and that of with a UDL over its entire length, is
explain: Deflection(Point) = WL³/48EI. Deflection(UDL) = 5WL³/384EI. The ratio is (1/48) / (5/384) = 8/5 = 24/15.

q: 13. The ratio of max deflection of a cantilever beam with an isolated load at free end and with a UDL over its entire length, is
explain: Deflection(Point) = WL³/3EI. Deflection(UDL) = WL³/8EI. The ratio is (1/3) / (1/8) = 8/3.

q: 14. Maximum deflection of a cantilever due to pure bending moment M at its free end, is
explain: Using the moment-area method, the deflection at the free end for a constant moment M is ML² / 2EI.

q: 15. A cantilever beam... load at free end. If the width of the beam is doubled, the deflection... will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Deflection is inversely proportional to Moment of Inertia (I). For a rectangle, I = bd³/12. If width 'b' is doubled, I doubles, and deflection becomes 1/2.

q: 16. If the length of a cantilever carrying an isolated load at its free end is doubled, the deflection... will increase by
explain: Deflection is proportional to L³. If length L is doubled, deflection increases by 2³ = 8 times.

q: 17. If the width of a simply supported beam carrying an isolated load at its centre is doubled, the deflection... is changed by
explain: Since deflection is inversely proportional to I (and thus width b), doubling the width reduces the deflection to half (1/2).

q: 18. If the depth of a simply supported beam carrying an isolated load at its centre, is doubled, the deflection... will be changed by a factor of
explain: Deflection is inversely proportional to I, which is proportional to d³. Doubling depth d makes deflection 1 / (2³) = 1/8.

q: 19. If the width b and depth d of a beam simply supported with a central load are interchanged, the deflection... will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Deflection 1 ∝ 1/(bd³). Deflection 2 ∝ 1/(db³). Ratio Δ2/Δ1 = (bd³) / (db³) = d²/b² = (d/b)².

q: 20. The maximum deflection of a cantilever beam of length l with a point load W at the free end is
explain: The standard formula for maximum deflection at the free end of a cantilever with a point load is Wl³ / 3EI.

q: 21. The maximum deflection of a fixed beam of length l carrying a central point load W is
explain: The deflection of a fixed beam is 1/4th of the deflection of a simply supported beam of the same span and load. Since SS beam deflection is Wl³/48EI, fixed beam deflection is Wl³/192EI.

q: 22. A beam which is fixed at one end and free at the other is called
explain: A cantilever is a rigid structural element that extends horizontally and is supported at only one end.

q: 23. A beam extending beyond the support is called
explain: An overhanging beam has one or both of its end portions extending beyond the supports.

q: 24. A beam encastered at both the ends is called
explain: A fixed beam (also known as a built-in or encastered beam) has both ends restrained against rotation and displacement.

q: 25. A beam supported on more than two supports is called
explain: A continuous beam is a statically indeterminate structure that spans across more than two supports.

q: 26. A cantilever beam is one which is
options: fixed at one end and free at the other end
supported on more than two supports
explain: The defining characteristic of a cantilever is the single fixed support that provides all the necessary stability.

q: 27. A continuous beam is one which is
options: fixed at one end and free at the other end
supported on more than two supports
explain: Any beam having three or more supports is classified as a continuous beam.

q: 28. A concentrated load is one which
options: acts at a point on a beam
spreads non-uniformly over the whole length
spreads uniformly over the whole length
varies uniformly over the whole length
explain: A concentrated or point load is assumed to act at a single specific point on the beam's axis.

q: 29. The bending moment on a section is maximum where shear force is
explain: Since dM/dx = V, the maximum bending moment occurs where the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign.

q: 30. The bending moment at the free end of a cantilever beam is
explain: Since there are no forces or moments acting beyond the free end, the internal bending moment at that point must be zero.

q: 31. The shear force of a cantilever beam of length l carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load on the beam is w * l. To maintain equilibrium, the vertical reaction (Shear Force) at the fixed end must equal the total load.

q: 32. The shear force diagram of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length will be
explain: The SF varies linearly from zero at the free end to wl at the fixed end, forming a right-angled triangle.

q: 33. The bending moment of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the free end.
explain: As per the definition of Bending Moment, the sum of moments of forces to the right of the free end is zero.

q: 34. The shear force and bending moment are zero at the free end of a cantilever beam, if it carries a
options: point load at the free end
point load at the middle of its length
uniformly distributed load over the whole length
explain: If a load is at the middle, the section from the middle to the free end has no load acting on it, resulting in zero SF and BM in that portion.

q: 35. The bending moment of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load is 'wl' acting at its center of gravity (l/2 from the support). Moment = (wl) * (l/2) = wl²/2.

q: 36. The shear force of a cantilever beam... carrying a gradually varying load from zero at the free end and w per unit length at the fixed end is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load is the area of the triangular loading diagram: 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * l * w = wl/2.

q: 37. The bending moment of a cantilever beam... carrying a gradually varying load from zero at free end and w per unit length at the fixed end is... at the fixed end.
explain: Total load wl/2 acts at a distance of l/3 from the base (fixed end). Moment = (wl/2) * (l/3) = wl²/6.

q: 38. The maximum bending moment of a simply supported beam of span l and carrying a point load w at the centre of beam, is
explain: Reaction at each support is w/2. Maximum BM at the center = (w/2) * (l/2) = wl/4.

q: 39. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam loaded in its centre is
explain: The BM increases linearly from zero at both supports to wl/4 at the center, forming an isosceles triangle.

q: 40. The shear force in the centre of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, is
explain: For a symmetrical UDL on an SS beam, the SF diagram passes through zero at the mid-span.

q: 41. The bending moment in the centre of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is
explain: The reaction is wl/2. BM at center = (wl/2 * l/2) - (w * l/2 * l/4) = wl²/4 - wl²/8 = wl²/8.

q: 42. The shear force at the ends of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is
options: wl at one end and -wl at the other end
wl/2 at one end and -wl/2 at the other end
wl²/2 at one end and -wl²/2 at the other end
explain: For a symmetrical UDL, each support reaction is half the total load (W = wl). Therefore, the shear force starts at +wl/2 at one support and ends at -wl/2 at the other.

q: 43. The bending moment diagram for a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, will be
explain: Since the shear force varies linearly (1st degree) for a UDL, the bending moment (which is the integral of SF) varies parabolically (2nd degree).

q: 44. The shear force at the centre of a simply supported beam with a gradually varying load from zero at both ends to w per metre at the centre, is
explain: Due to the symmetry of the triangular loading (zero at ends, max at center), the shear force at the exact mid-point of the span must be zero.

q: 45. The point of contra flexure is a point where
explain: The point of contraflexure (or inflection) is the location in a structural member where the bending moment changes from positive (sagging) to negative (hogging) or vice versa.

q: 46. When shear force at a point is zero, then bending moment is... at that point.
explain: Mathematically, V = dM/dx. If the derivative (V) is zero, the function (M) is at a local maximum or minimum.

q: 47. When there is a sudden increase or decrease in shear force diagram between any two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: A vertical jump in the shear force diagram always corresponds to the application of a concentrated (point) load at 그 point.

q: 48. When the shear force diagram is a parabolic curve between two points, it indicates that there is a
options: point load at the two points
no loading between the two points
uniformly distributed load between the two points
uniformly varying load between the two points
explain: If the loading is linear (uniformly varying), the shear force (its integral) will be a 2nd-degree parabolic curve.

q: 49. In a beam where shear force changes sign, the bending moment will be
explain: A change in sign in the SFD indicates that the SF passes through zero, which identifies the location of the maximum bending moment.

q: 50. The number of reaction components possible at a fixed or built in end for a general loading
explain: A fixed support prevents all movement (vertical, horizontal, and rotation), providing three reactions: vertical force, horizontal force, and a bending moment.
